name: Sublime Chord
body:
A sublime chord believes music expresses the deep mathematical harmony underlying reality, and by studying song, mathematics, and the movements of the stars they unlock powerful magical truths known as the First Song. Though often trained as bards, they abandon further bardic study to pursue greater arcane power and knowledge, frequently acting as scholarly seekers of lost lore and cosmic mysteries.

Hit Die: d8

Requirements

To qualify to become a sublime chord, a character must fulfill all of the following criteria:

Skills: Knowledge (Arcana) 10 ranks, Perception 10 ranks, Perform (any) 10 ranks, Profession (astrologer) 3 ranks, Spellcraft 3 ranks

Spells: Able to cast 3rd-level spells

Special: Bardic performance, raging song, or similar performance-related ability

Class Skills

The sublime chord’s class skills (and the key ability for each skill) are Craft, Diplomacy, Knowledge (all), Linguistics, Perception, Perform, Profession, and Spellcraft.

Skill Points at Each Level: 4 + Int modifier.

Class Features

The following are class features of the sublime chord.

Weapon and Armor Proficiency

Sublime chords gain no proficiency with any weapon or armor.

Sublime Music (Su)

Trained in the arts of song and spell, the sublime chord counts their sublime chord level as levels in classes which possess bardic performance, raging song, or other abilities they may have which is similar (such as the argent performance from the argent dramaturge prestige class.) In addition the sublime chord increases their caster level as per normal prestige classes with spellcasting (receiving +1 Spells per Day per level of existing class similar to how other prestige classes do). This is not listed in the table above due to the additional spell levels, but otherwise is present.

Sublime chords have the ability to cast spells stronger than their normal repertoire, they continue being able to cast spells from their normal spell list along with spells from a higher spell level. This counts as their original progression, plus gaining additional spells known depending on their type of spellcasting. Arcane spellcasters learn sublime chord spells from the sorcerer/wizard spell list, divine spellcasters learn from the cleric/oracle spell list, and psychic spellcasters learn from the psychic spell list.

They cast these spells similar to the spells of their original class of the highest level they possessed before starting to take sublime chord levels.

Song of Arcane Power (Sp)

At 2nd level a sublime chord can learn to use their bardic performances to assist in spellcasting. As a move action, they can prepare to channel the song of power into the spell. To do this, they make a Perform check with a DC = 10 + 1/2 the sublime chord’s caster level + spell level. On a successful perform check this grants a +1 to the spell’s caster level, and this bonus increases by 1 for every 5 the check beats the DC by. This spell must be cast by the end of the sublime chord’s next turn or else the song fades and the benefit is wasted. This expends rounds of the sublime chord’s bardic performance equal to half the spell level (minimum of 1).

Discordant Melody (Su)

At 3rd level the sublime chord learns to channel raw might into their spells which echo with raw magic vibrations. The first time damage is dealt with a spell you deal an additional die of damage equal to your caster level (maximum of 20 additional damage dice). Alternatively, they can alter a spell which normally deals energy damage to deal sonic damage. If this is used, the spell only gains an additional die of damage equal to half your caster level (maximum of 10 additional damage dice).

Note: This works on spell-like abilities as well, but the spell-like ability must be an effect dealing energy damage.

Uneven Tempo (Su)

At 4th level the sublime chord learns to act in ways that are unpredictable, just like their music. When rolling initiative, the sublime chord can choose to evoke uneven tempo and split their initiative into two: their original roll – 5, and their original roll – 10. They share their actions across both initiative turns, and despite having two turns this does not speed up actions listed as taking “1 round” or longer. While under the effects of haste, the sublime chord has three initiatives with the third being at their original roll -20. While under the effects of slow, they only have their one turn (alongside the other effects of slow).

Rhymes of the Soul (Su)

At 5th level the sublime chord is capable of putting together tunes and beats which correspond with another person’s innate biorhythm. While using their bardic performance (or equivalent effect) the sublime chord can choose someone under its effect who can see and hear them and who has taken their turn already. By spending a standard action they can choose to make a Perform check against the target (DC 10 + target’s HD + target’s Charisma modifier) and on a success the target on their turn receives a second move action on their turn (similar to a quick runner’s shirt) and allies can only benefit from this once per day and its effects cannot be coupled with similar effects like the quick runner’s shirt. Doing this expends 2 rounds of bardic performance.

Song of Timelessness (Sp)

At 6th level the sublime chord can spend a standard action to envelop a single creature within 60 feet who they can see in a field of timelessness. This creature must make a Will save (DC 10 + 1/2 sublime chord’s total level + Charisma modifier) and on a failed save the target is frozen in place by this shimmering aura. No force can effect them while afflicted; weapons fail to reach them, spells fail to target them, and if the ground were destroyed beneath them they’d remain frozen in place as if stuck in time. This lasts for the duration of the sublime chord’s performance or 1 minute per sublime chord level (whichever comes first) and upon ending the subject immediately returns to normal. As far as they’re concerned, no time seems to have passed. In order to use this ability the sublime chord must currently be in the midst of a bardic performance or similar ability.

Heaven and Earth (Su)

At 7th level the sublime chord’s music is able to reach even those who are incapable of hearing or seeing it. Physical barriers do not prevent individuals from benefitting from their performance, and needn’t hear and see the sublime chord to be targeted, however they must be able to perceive them with one sense. Thus; if they cannot be heard they must at least be able to see the target, if neither are available they must be able to smell the target or sense them through another means (for example, tremorsense).

First Song (Sp)

At 8th level the sublime chord learns to utilize the first song to emanate powers of pure creation and in turn, shape the world as they please. This allows the sublime chord to cast fabricate and polymorph any object by spending 4 rounds of bardic performance to do so. The sublime chord can utilize song of arcane power to instead increase the duration factor of polymorph any object if they choose to use it in this way.

Assemble Masterpiece (Su)

At 9th level the sublime chord has studied so deeply into the intricacies of mystic music they can begin formulating their own. This functions per the rules to research a new spell except the sublime chord is capable of researching the creation of new masterpieces they can use and benefit from.

Song of the Cosmic Fire (Sp)

At 10th level the sublime chord can spend 4 uses of bardic performance to as a standard action create a pillar at a point within 200 feet of them which they have line of effect to and from that point a 20-foot-radius pillar raises up 20 feet high. The sublime chord makes a Perform check and creatures in the area of the spell must make a Reflex save (DC 10 + 1/2 total level + Charisma modifier) versus damage equal to the result of the sublime chord’s Perform check result. This damage is untyped, but against creatures with vulnerability to fire it counts as fire damage. Creatures who succeed their reflex save take half damage. Evasion and improved evasion work against this as normal.
